title: Automating Daily LinkedIn Drafts from GitHub
angle: Built a GitHub Action that selects a repo, uses Groq LLM for copy, renders code-snippet images, and sends drafts via Telegram.
post:
I was spending 15 minutes every morning copying code snippets into LinkedIn drafts - until I let a GitHub Action handle it.

The repo github-to-linkedin-poster runs daily at 08:00 UAE, picks one of my repositories, asks Groq to write a post, renders a highlighted code image, and pushes the draft to Telegram.

-> The workflow pulls raw LLM output and isolates the `POST:` section, trimming whitespace and limiting length to stay within LinkedIn’s character cap.
-> It extracts the `FILE:` and `LINES:` markers, then reads the source file from the repo’s file map.
-> To keep images readable, the snippet is capped at 20 lines and excess indentation is stripped before highlighting.
-> The final HTML/CSS is sent to hcti.io, which returns a PNG that the Telegram bot delivers.

Balancing automation with readability meant adding safety checks - like ignoring empty snippets and enforcing a minimum line count - so every draft looks polished without manual tweaks.

How do you handle content length limits when generating posts from code automatically?
